clue.text: Chap going to kiss girl modelling art wear gets the bird

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: modelling clay means shaping it anew, so the letters that follow are reshaped

parts.note: X is the kiss at the end of a letter
a girl is referred to as she
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man kisses a girl who is modelling clothes, and the audience boos him off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' is the idiom for being jeered, which hides the plain definition 'bird' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx shearwater is a seabird of the Atlantic, named after the Isle of Man where it once bred in great numbers.

clue.text: Mary familiar with battlefield in book

parts.note: Moll is a pet form of the name Mary
Flanders was the great Western Front battlefield of the First World War

explanation.surface: A woman called Mary, well acquainted with a battlefield, appears in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar' here means a familiar (pet) form of the name, not 'acquainted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moll Flanders is Daniel Defoe's 1722 novel about a thief and adventuress, so it is a book title.

clue.text: Partly train a director to cope with bottom of recession, perhaps

indicators.note: partly says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters lying inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of train, the word a and the start of director

explanation.surface: Training a company director to handle the worst point of an economic slump.
explanation.definitionFit: A nadir is the lowest point of anything, so the trough of a recession is an example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Poem about bun involved a summer hat

indicators.note: about means going round, so the poem wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so its letters come out in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem about a bun was part of a summer, it seems, like a light-verse cookbook.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled bun goes in after the first letter of the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbonnet is a wide-brimmed cloth hat worn to shade the face and neck in hot weather.

clue.text: Promised to become enmeshed

definitions.meaning: second meaning: locked together, as the teeth of gears are

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a commitment that turns into a trap; the two meanings are betrothal and gears meshing.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothed couple are engaged, and gear wheels whose teeth interlock are said to be engaged or meshed.

clue.text: Right hand turn Jag takes in garden

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
H is the abbreviation for hand
a U-turn, so turn can stand for the letter U
a jag is a sharp projecting point, as is a barb

explanation.surface: A Jaguar car swings right into a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Jag looks like the car but is a sharp point; the definition is loose, naming where the plant grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is a common vegetable-garden plant grown for its edible pink stalks, so it belongs in a garden.

clue.text: Sailor takes governor to church

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A sailor escorts the governor to a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a monastery's church, often a large one such as Westminster Abbey, so it names a church.

clue.text: It's a fair bet doctor takes old French soldier to flat

parts.note: a flat surface is even
MO is a medical officer
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A doctor brings an old French veteran back to his apartment, a reasonable gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor and the soldier join first, then go after the word for flat, which comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Even money is betting odds of one to one, where the stake is matched, so it is a fair, balanced wager.

clue.text: Having taken on cargo at lake port…

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship loading cargo at a lakeside harbour, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A laden ship is loaded, carrying a full burden of freight, which is what taking on cargo produces.

clue.text: …dirty child on platform is even more dirty

parts.note: a grub is a grubby small child
a bier is the platform a coffin rests on

explanation.surface: A grimy child standing on a stage gets filthier still.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby means dirty, and the comparative form expresses a greater degree of grime than before.

clue.text: Boy game to help people across the Thames

definitions.note: a descriptive definition of what the thing does

parts.note: Albert is a boy's name
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A lad plays a game to raise money for people crossing the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames is the river through London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Albert Bridge is a London road crossing over the Thames at Chelsea, so it carries people over the river.

clue.text: Characteristic of Persian cat in the distance?

definitions.note: read as two words, fur long
definitions.meaning: first reading: split into two words, describing the breed's coat
second meaning: a measure of length

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two and it describes a Persian cat's coat; whole, it is a unit of length, an eighth of a mile, used in horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlong is a unit of length of 220 yards, still used for racecourse distances.

clue.text: Unfathomable element in baby's maltreatment

indicators.note: an element in something is one component of it, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the run begins after the first letter and crosses into the second word

explanation.surface: Something deep and unexplained lies behind a case of child abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal originally meant bottomless, like an abyss, so it can mean too deep to be fathomed or measured.

clue.text: Account not rendered by historian

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account

indicators.note: rendered means made over or melted down, so the word before it is recast in new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A historian failed to submit his expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not rendered' reads as 'not submitted', but rendered is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Acton was a Victorian English historian, remembered for saying that power tends to corrupt.

clue.text: Drag Wendy Hiller to place of execution

parts.note: to drag something along is to tow it

indicators.note: the name is read as wend-y, wending or winding about, so the next word's letters wander

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pulling the actress Wendy Hiller off to be beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Wendy Hiller was an English film actress; her first name doubles as a jokey signal for winding letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower Hill, beside the Tower of London, was the site of public beheadings of traitors and nobles.

clue.text: Society girl meeting poet in tube, perhaps

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside another

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet

indicators.note: perhaps marks a loose version of the word before it, so its letters may be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A society girl bumping into a poet on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled tube goes inside the poet, after the first letter, though the clue's word order suggests the opposite way round. The Tube is the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young upper-class woman making her first formal appearance in fashionable society.

clue.text: Club official sure in re art anyway

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the letters that follow
anyway means in any manner at all, so the letters can go in any order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A club official who is confident about matters of art, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Re is the business-letter word for 'concerning'; here it is simply letters to shuffle with art.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer of a club or society in charge of its funds and accounts.

clue.text: Dispense with outdoor party?

parts.note: a do is a party
without is an old word for outside, out of doors

explanation.surface: Cancel the garden party?
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads backwards: party first, then outdoor.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense with something is to manage without it, to forgo having it at all.

clue.text: Lasted longer than couple embraced by roué, perhaps

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside another's arms, so these letters go inside
perhaps marks a loose version of the word before it, so its letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, accent dropped, to be rearranged
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A rake outlasted a couple he had in his arms.
explanation.walkthrough: A roué is a dissolute older man, a rake.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to outlast it, still going after the other has worn out.

clue.text: Managed to take back outside most of the crosspiece

indicators.note: outside puts the word around the letters for managed
taking something back retraces it, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: Managing to reclaim most of a horizontal beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' looks like a deletion, but the whole word most is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal bar across a window or above a door, a structural crosspiece.

clue.text: Country where, for example, youth leader takes little part

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of youth
PT is a short form of part

explanation.surface: A country where a youth leader plays only a small role.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is the North African nation on the Nile, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Seldom met with portion of food

parts.note: what is seldom met with is rare
a bit is a portion

explanation.surface: An unusual serving of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rabbit, is melted cheese on toast, a savoury dish to eat.

clue.text: Tired after stroke to point

parts.note: a stroke is a blow
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Exhausted after a rowing stroke to the finishing point.
explanation.definitionFit: A blown horse or runner is out of breath and spent, so blown means exhausted.

clue.text: He tries to give confidence to underwriter

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who provides life assurance

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an insurance salesman reassuring a client; the two senses are a reassurer and an insurer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who assures gives people confidence, and in insurance an assurer underwrites policies, especially life cover.

clue.text: Sailors holding girl up to see bird

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so the sailors surround the girl

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Sailors lift a girl up so she can watch a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Fearful of being socially acceptable in island circles

parts.note: Timor is an island in South-East Asia

indicators.note: circles here is a verb, surrounding or ringing what is inside

parts.note: circles look like the letter O, plural
U means upper class, socially acceptable, as opposed to non-U

explanation.surface: Nervous about being accepted among island social circles.
explanation.walkthrough: Circles does double duty: it supplies the round letters and tells you they go around the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Timorous means timid and easily frightened, a close synonym of fearful.

clue.text: Waxed enthusiastic about figure in a red jacket

indicators.note: a jacket wraps round its wearer, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
V is the Roman numeral five, a figure

explanation.surface: Someone gushed about a figure wearing a red coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to talk with wild enthusiasm, so waxing enthusiastic about something is raving.

clue.text: Fruit to place round kitchen fireplace

parts.note: Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire, also a battle site
a round letter
a range is a large old kitchen stove set in the fireplace

explanation.surface: Fruit being placed round the kitchen hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange' looks like it should be the fruit, but the fruit is the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim Orange is an old English variety of eating and cooking apple, so it is a fruit.
